          Files.need(options["out"] && (options.keys-%w[out keys]).empty? && options["keys"].empty?,
            "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_OFFLINE_OPTIONS")
          $stdout.write(Files.json(reopen(options["out"])))
          return 0
        end
        if %w[receive copy].include?(command)
          allowed = command == "copy" ? %w[delivery manifest keys out] : %w[delivery manifest keys]
          Files.need(options["delivery"] && HASH.match?(options["manifest"].to_s) &&
            (options.keys-allowed).empty? && options["keys"].empty? &&
            (command != "copy" || options["out"]), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_OFFLINE_OPTIONS")
          value = if command == "receive"
            receive_application(options.fetch("delivery"),expected_manifest_sha256: options.fetch("manifest"))
          else
            copy_application(options.fetch("delivery"),expected_manifest_sha256: options.fetch("manifest"),
              out: options.fetch("out"))
          end
          $stdout.write(Files.json(value))
          return 0
        end
        Files.need(%w[out room source_key dataset_id native_manifest checkout python node].all? { |key| options[key] } &&
          (options.keys-%w[out room source_key dataset_id native_manifest checkout python node keys]).empty? &&
          HASH.match?(options["native_manifest"].to_s), "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_LIFECYCLE_SELECTION")

        cancellation = Object.new
        cancellation.define_singleton_method(:cancelled?) { interrupted }
        old_int = Signal.trap("INT") { interrupted = true }
        old_term = Signal.trap("TERM") { interrupted = true }
        begin
          $stdout.write(Files.json(run(options,cancellation)))
          0
        ensure
          Signal.trap("INT",old_int)
          Signal.trap("TERM",old_term)
        end
      ensure
        File.umask(old_umask)
      end
    rescue Starforge::Error, RailsDataset::ImportError, OptionParser::ParseError => error
      $stderr.write(JSON.generate({"error"=>error.respond_to?(:code) ? error.code : "RUBY_NATIVE_DATASET_LIFECYCLE_OPTIONS",
        "details"=>error.respond_to?(:details) ? error.details : {}})+"\n")
      2
    end
  end
end
exit Starforge::NativeDatasetLifecycle.main(ARGV.dup) if File.expand_path($PROGRAM_NAME) == File.expand_path(__FILE__)

# Import complete dataset editions into an existing Rails application

This example turns an original received SF88/SF100 dataset into a reviewed, repeatable database import. It includes the migration, application models, field mapping, background job and commissioning command. The importer keeps the application's existing tenant relation, target records, database connection and native dataset source together.

A complete preview shows every incoming and removed key. Committing that selected preview writes all target changes, current key state, original source rows, edition history and the final receipt in one Active Record transaction. A repeated business operation key reopens its original committed result.

## Install the application side

Use Ruby 3.1 or newer, Rails/Active Record 7.1 or newer and the application's existing database. The merchant package already includes the Ruby standard-library reader and source-bound Dataset receiving client. The application adds Active Record and Active Job through its normal Rails bundle.

Copy the example migration into the application's migration directory with an unused timestamp and run the application's usual migration command. The migration creates four import/history tables and one example target table:

| Table | Stored application state |
| --- | --- |
| starforge_dataset_streams | Tenant/name identity, source/key/scope bindings, current revision and latest edition |
| starforge_dataset_editions | Stable operation identity, selected preview and complete committed receipt |
| starforge_dataset_rows | Current exact source key, original target ID, active/removed state and last source values |
| starforge_dataset_entries | Every edition's original JSON row, exact changes, target ID and source position |
| starforge_dataset_catalog_records | Example tenant-scoped business records with an actual unique source key |

~~~sh
dataset_package=/absolute/customer-package
cp "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/create_dataset_import_tables.rb" \
  db/migrate/20261012085000_create_dataset_import_tables.rb
bin/rails db:migrate
install -d -m 0700 tmp/dataset-review
~~~

Choose a new migration timestamp if that path already exists. Keep the delivered package hierarchy intact: the example models load the verified importer through its relative package path.

For a customer's established schema, keep the four history tables and replace the example CatalogRecord with the application's original model. The relation passed to RailsDataset must already enforce the authenticated tenant's record scope. The stream and all four model classes must use the very same Active Record connection pool. Add or retain a real unique index covering the selected key within that scope; for this example it is tenant_key plus external_id.

The model examples make completed editions and source entries immutable through normal Active Record writes. The stream and current-key state advance as later complete editions are committed. Retain all four history tables with the application's regular database backups.

## Receive the original complete dataset

Follow the merchant package's [Dataset receiving guide](../../DATASETS.md) to prepare, review, acquire or attach, receive, and reopen the original dataset. Retain its actual dataset-customer.json SHA-256 with the application import record.

The Rails side opens that completed directory offline. The receiving reader checks every required original file, whole-file byte count and SHA-256, final native status, full page/row range and projected field set before yielding rows. It parses original integer tokens as Ruby Integer and decimal tokens as BigDecimal; the original JSON spelling and row order remain available for each row.

The same completed packet can be reopened by a background job. Each iteration reads a private immutable verified snapshot. Original payment review, native acquisition and recovery belong to the existing merchant Dataset client.

## Map the customer's real fields

Copy mapping.json into the application's configuration and change its field names to the actual received dataset. Remove unused example mappings. Every mapped source field must appear in the received manifest's projected fields.

The included mapping expects these example source names: id, name, amount, quantity, active, observed_on and recorded_at. Their names are application examples; inspect the actual delivery's fields before selecting them:

~~~ruby
delivery = Starforge::DatasetDelivery.open(
  "/absolute/private/received-dataset",
  expected_manifest_sha256: actual_manifest_sha256
)
puts JSON.pretty_generate(delivery.fields)
~~~

The mapping has three decisions:

| Setting | Result |
| --- | --- |
| key_columns | Exact stable business key; one or several mapped target columns |
| columns | Source field and explicit native target type for each managed attribute |
| removal | Retain missing records, or set a separate Boolean archive column inactive |

Supported target types are string/text, integer, decimal, Boolean, date and datetime. A source integer stays exact. A decimal string or native decimal token is accepted only when the target column preserves its value and range. A datetime must carry an explicit UTC or numeric offset and fit the database column's precision. Date strings use YYYY-MM-DD. Boolean fields accept actual true/false values.

A string column accepts a string by default. Set stringify to true only when the application intentionally converts a numeric or Boolean source value to its literal text. Stable keys retain capitalization, whitespace and leading zeroes supplied as strings.

For each mapping, null is assign or preserve; missing is error or preserve. These are independent choices. Key columns always require an actual value. The original SF100 reader supplies the complete projected row shape, and a field left out of the application's mapping remains application-owned. Explicit null assignments must fit the target column's null constraint. Target primary keys, timestamps, lock versions, STI columns and fixed scope attributes cannot be overwritten by source mapping.

The supplied archive policy uses source_active:

~~~json
{
  "strategy": "archive",
  "column": "source_active",
  "active": true,
  "inactive": false
}
~~~

A key absent from a later complete selected dataset becomes removed in the import state and its original target record receives source_active=false. If the key reappears, its record becomes active and the preview reports restored. With {"strategy":"retain"}, removal changes the import history while preserving the target record's attributes.

Removals are calculated from previously managed active keys in this exact stream. The importer requires the original complete selection: a final native snapshot, original merchant contract, operation, resolved endpoint, selected query and tenant scope. Page cursor, page size and dataset snapshot can change as the same selected dataset advances. Changing the merchant contract, dataset endpoint, key definition or selected membership requires an explicit application migration or another authorized stream.

## Create the stable stream and review the complete edition

Run commissioning through the actual Rails application's runner so the original database and model configuration are loaded. Paths below are templates for the customer's retained package, received delivery, configuration and private output directory.

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" init -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog

bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" preview -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

The preview command writes the entire JSON and CSV revision into files named by its full preview SHA-256. It also prints counts and the exact output descriptors. Every preview entry includes:

- Original source ordinal, original JSON line and row SHA-256.
- Exact stable key and existing native target ID.
- Inserted, updated, unchanged or removed action.
- Adopted existing record, restored key and changed-source indicators.
- Exact before/after values and the selected target's current version fingerprint.

The complete JSON uses tagged values for precise types. For example, ["integer","9007199254740993"] is an exact integer, ["decimal","12.34000001"] is an exact decimal, ["null"] is explicit null, and ["datetime","2026-10-12T08:00:00.000000000Z"] is a UTC instant. The original unmodified source JSON is retained beside those mapped values.

Review all changes through these files or embed Preview.each_entry in the application's existing review screen. The neutral JSON/CSV surfaces carry the full dataset; the printed summary provides navigation and the selected hash. No preview is committed by creating or exporting it.

## Apply that selected preview

Use a persistent operation key from the application's own import/job record. Preserve that exact key and preview hash when a job retries.

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" commit -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --operation catalog-edition-2026-10-12 \
  --preview-sha256 ACTUAL_COMPLETE_PREVIEW_SHA256 \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

The importer locks the stream, rebuilds the complete current preview and compares it to the selected hash. It then saves the actual application models using their normal validations and callbacks, verifies the stored mapped values and scope, and commits the target updates plus complete edition history together. A changed target, changed stream revision or changed source/mapping produces a fresh-preview requirement before any edition is applied. Database/model validation failures roll back the whole transaction.

If a process exits after the database commit but before exporting its receipt, the same command with the original operation and preview returns that already committed edition and recreates its complete receipt export. Using that operation key for another source, mapping or preview is rejected.

The importer owns its database transaction boundary. Call it outside another open application transaction. Use database-side work or the application's after_commit/outbox arrangement for external effects in model callbacks. Active Record documents [transaction scope and callback behavior](https://api.rubyonrails.org/v7.1.0/classes/ActiveRecord/Transactions/ClassMethods.html) and [row locking with with_lock](https://api.rubyonrails.org/v7.1.0/classes/ActiveRecord/Locking/Pessimistic.html).

## Use the actual application job

The provided ImportDatasetJob consumes an already received complete packet and selected application preview. Resolve tenant identity and paths within the authenticated application, then enqueue the stable values:

~~~ruby
Starforge::DatasetExample::ImportDatasetJob.perform_later(
  stream_id: stream.id,
  tenant_key: current_account.dataset_tenant_key,
  delivery_directory: import_record.received_directory,
  manifest_sha256: import_record.dataset_manifest_sha256,
  mapping_path: Rails.root.join("config", "dataset-catalog-mapping.json").to_s,
  operation_key: import_record.operation_key,
  preview_sha256: import_record.selected_preview_sha256,
  receipt_path: import_record.receipt_path
)
~~~

Require the delivered job from an application initializer, for example require "/absolute/customer-package/examples/rails_dataset/import_dataset_job". To move it into the application's normal autoload paths, move its model classes with it and update the relative require to their actual location. The importer takes those classes explicitly:

~~~ruby
importer = Starforge::RailsDataset.new(
  delivery: delivery,
  scope: current_account.catalog_records,
  stream: stream,
  models: {edition: DatasetEdition, row: DatasetRow, entry: DatasetEntry},
  mapping: mapping
)
preview = importer.preview
begin
  File.open(review_path, "wb") { |io| preview.write_json(io) }
  selected_hash = preview.sha256
ensure
  preview.close
end
# Persist selected_hash with the application review decision, then use it:
receipt = importer.import!(
  operation_key: import_record.operation_key,
  expected_preview_sha256: import_record.selected_preview_sha256
)
~~~

The source key is resolved against the real scoped target relation. An existing matching record can be adopted once; a record already managed by a different stream is rejected. If a tracked target has moved outside the authorized scope, the application must resolve that relationship before applying another edition. All new records inherit the fixed values from the original scope.

## Reopen a committed edition and continue revisions

The status command reads the current stream and complete active/removed key counts:

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" status -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog
~~~

The receipt command exports every retained entry from an existing operation, including original source JSON and exact before/after values:

~~~sh
bin/rails runner "$dataset_package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb" receipt -- \
  --tenant account-42 --stream merchant-catalog \
  --delivery /absolute/private/received-dataset \
  --manifest-sha256 ACTUAL_DATASET_CUSTOMER_MANIFEST_SHA256 \
  --mapping /absolute/application/config/dataset-catalog-mapping.json \
  --operation catalog-edition-2026-10-12 \
  --out /absolute/application/tmp/dataset-review
~~~

Reopen can use a current complete packet belonging to the same bound stream while exporting an earlier operation's saved source rows. The exporter checks every retained row hash, complete entry count and edition digest. All output writes are streamed into a private temporary file; an interrupted export can be repeated, and an existing path is accepted only when its full bytes match.

For the next original dataset edition, retain the same stream and stable key mapping, receive its complete packet, create a new application operation key, preview its entire diff and commit that selected preview. The existing target identities, source history and application records advance together.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Run through the original Rails application's bin/rails runner.
require "optparse"
require_relative "models"

module Starforge
  module DatasetExample
    module Commission
      module_function
      def run(arguments)
        options = {}
        parser = OptionParser.new do |o|
          o.banner = "bin/rails runner /absolute/package/examples/rails_dataset/commission.rb COMMAND -- [options]"
          o.separator "Commands: init, preview, commit, receipt, status"
          o.on("--tenant KEY", "Authenticated application's tenant key") { |v| options[:tenant] = v }
          o.on("--stream NAME", "Stable dataset stream within that tenant") { |v| options[:stream] = v }
          o.on("--delivery DIRECTORY", "Original complete received dataset") { |v| options[:delivery] = v }
          o.on("--manifest-sha256 SHA", "Selected dataset-customer.json SHA-256") { |v| options[:manifest] = v }
          o.on("--mapping PATH", "Application's explicit JSON field mapping") { |v| options[:mapping] = v }
          o.on("--out DIRECTORY", "Existing private complete-output directory") { |v| options[:out] = v }
          o.on("--operation KEY", "Stable application edition operation key") { |v| options[:operation] = v }
          o.on("--preview-sha256 SHA", "Exact full preview selected for commit") { |v| options[:preview] = v }
          o.on("-h", "--help") { puts o; return 0 }
        end
        command = arguments.shift
        if command.nil? || %w[-h --help].include?(command)
          puts parser
          return 0
        end
        # Rails runner retains all following arguments; accept its optional
        # delimiter without allowing unknown flags to disappear silently.
        arguments.shift if arguments.first == "--"
        parser.parse!(arguments)
        RailsDataset.need(arguments.empty? && %w[init preview commit receipt status].include?(command),
          "DATASET_COMMISSION_COMMAND")
        required = [:tenant, :stream]
        required += [:delivery, :manifest, :mapping] if %w[preview commit receipt].include?(command)
        required += [:out] if %w[preview receipt].include?(command)
        required += [:operation, :preview] if command == "commit"
        required += [:operation] if command == "receipt"
        required.each do |key|
          RailsDataset.need(options[key].is_a?(String) && !options[key].strip.empty?,
            "DATASET_COMMISSION_OPTION", option: key)
        end
        stream_scope = DatasetStream.where(tenant_key: options[:tenant], name: options[:stream])
        if command == "init"
          # The unique tenant/name index resolves concurrent job creation.
          stream = stream_scope.create_or_find_by!({})
          puts RailsDataset.json({"stream_id"=>stream.id.to_s, "tenant"=>stream.tenant_key,
            "name"=>stream.name, "revision"=>stream.revision})
          return 0
        end
        stream = stream_scope.take!
        if command == "status"
          editions = DatasetEdition.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id)
          puts RailsDataset.json({"stream_id"=>stream.id.to_s, "tenant"=>stream.tenant_key, "name"=>stream.name,
            "revision"=>stream.revision, "latest_edition_id"=>stream.latest_edition_id&.to_s,
            "target_model"=>stream.target_model, "scope_sha256"=>stream.scope_sha256,
            "key_mapping_sha256"=>stream.key_mapping_sha256, "membership_sha256"=>stream.membership_sha256,
            "editions"=>editions.count,
            "active_keys"=>DatasetRow.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id, status: "active").count,
            "removed_keys"=>DatasetRow.where(dataset_stream_id: stream.id, status: "removed").count})
          return 0
        end
        importer = DatasetExample.importer(stream: stream, tenant_key: options[:tenant],
          delivery_directory: options[:delivery], manifest_sha256: options[:manifest], mapping_path: options[:mapping])
        case command
        when "preview"
          directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
          preview = importer.preview
          begin
            stem = "preview-#{preview.sha256}"
            files = [
              Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory, "#{stem}.json")) { |io| preview.write_json(io) },
              Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory, "#{stem}.csv")) { |io| preview.write_csv(io) }
            ]
            puts RailsDataset.json(preview.summary.merge("outputs"=>files))
          ensure
            preview.close
          end
        when "commit"
          result = importer.import!(operation_key: options[:operation], expected_preview_sha256: options[:preview])
          if options[:out]
            directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
            name = "edition-#{result.fetch("revision")}-#{result.fetch("operation_sha256")}.json"
            output = Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory,name)) do |io|
              importer.write_receipt(io, operation_key: options[:operation])
            end
            result = result.merge("complete_receipt"=>output)
          end
          puts RailsDataset.json(result)
        when "receipt"
          directory = Files.directory(options[:out])
          result = importer.receipt(operation_key: options[:operation])
          name = "edition-#{result.fetch("revision")}-#{result.fetch("operation_sha256")}.json"
          output = Artifacts.write_once(File.join(directory,name)) do |io|
            importer.write_receipt(io, operation_key: options[:operation])
          end
          puts RailsDataset.json(result.merge("complete_receipt"=>output))
        end
        0
      rescue Starforge::Error, RailsDataset::ImportError, OptionParser::ParseError => error
        warn JSON.generate({"error"=>error.respond_to?(:code) ? error.code : error.class.name,
          "details"=>error.respond_to?(:details) ? error.details : {"message"=>error.message}})
        2
      end
    end
  end
end

exit Starforge::DatasetExample::Commission.run(ARGV.dup) if File.expand_path($PROGRAM_NAME) == File.expand_path(__FILE__)

# MIT. Copy these models into the same database as the original target records.
require_relative "../../rails_dataset"

module Starforge
  module DatasetExample
    class Record < ActiveRecord::Base
      self.abstract_class = true
    end

    class DatasetStream < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_streams"
      validates :tenant_key, :name, presence: true
    end

    class DatasetEdition < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_editions"
      before_update do
        if receipt_sha256_in_database.present?
          raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "A committed dataset edition is immutable"
        end
      end
      before_destroy { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "Retain dataset edition history" }
    end

    class DatasetRow < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_rows"
      validates :status, inclusion: {in: %w[active removed]}
    end

    class DatasetEntry < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_entries"
      before_update { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "A dataset entry is immutable" }
      before_destroy { raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord, "Retain dataset source rows" }
    end

    class CatalogRecord < Record
      self.table_name = "starforge_dataset_catalog_records"
      validates :tenant_key, :external_id, presence: true
    end

    MODELS = {edition: DatasetEdition, row: DatasetRow, entry: DatasetEntry}.freeze

    def self.importer(stream:, tenant_key:, delivery_directory:, manifest_sha256:, mapping_path:)
      RailsDataset.need(stream.tenant_key == tenant_key, "DATASET_EXAMPLE_TENANT")
      delivery = DatasetDelivery.open(delivery_directory, expected_manifest_sha256: manifest_sha256)
      mapping = Files.parse(Files.read(mapping_path))
      RailsDataset.new(delivery: delivery, scope: CatalogRecord.where(tenant_key: tenant_key),
        stream: stream, models: MODELS, mapping: mapping)
    end

    # Stream a complete output into a new file. A retry accepts only the exact
    # original bytes; it never replaces another review or completed receipt.
    module Artifacts
      module_function
      def write_once(path)
        path = File.expand_path(path)
        directory = Files.directory(File.dirname(path))
        temp = Tempfile.new([".dataset-artifact-", ".pending"], directory)
        begin
          temp.binmode
          yield temp
          temp.flush
          temp.fsync
          count, digest = temp.size, Digest::SHA256.file(temp.path).hexdigest
          temp.close
          begin
            File.link(temp.path, path)
            Files.sync(directory)
          rescue Errno::EEXIST
            # Preview/history exports can be larger than one original data file.
            # Verify all bytes directly without imposing the native input ceiling.
            File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::NONBLOCK) do |file|
              before = file.stat
              Files.need(before.file? && before.size == count, "DATASET_ARTIFACT_CONFLICT")
              actual, received = Digest::SHA256.new, 0
              while (chunk = file.read(1_048_576))
                actual.update(chunk)
                received += chunk.bytesize
                Files.need(received <= count, "DATASET_ARTIFACT_CONFLICT")
              end
              after = file.stat
              Files.need(received == count && actual.hexdigest == digest &&
                [before.dev,before.ino,before.size,before.mtime,before.ctime] ==
                [after.dev,after.ino,after.size,after.mtime,after.ctime], "DATASET_ARTIFACT_CONFLICT")
            end
          end
          {"path"=>path, "bytes"=>count, "sha256"=>digest}
        ensure
          temp.close!
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

# Dataset operator for the original Rails application

This package adds a complete, server-rendered dataset receiving and import interface to Rails. An operator selects a received delivery, reviews every row and the configured mapping, approves the exact preview, and imports an edition through the application's original Active Record models. Original attachments, every historical receipt and a complete review handoff remain available.

The interface uses neutral grayscale styles and ordinary HTML forms. It includes the source inbox, complete paginated change review and filters, typed before/after values, original source JSON, background preparation/import, retry of the same operation, refresh from the review's saved source, edition history, original file downloads, and full JSON/CSV/TAR exports.

## Use the complete Baserow customer package

The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge baserow-source customer --help
~~~

The provider's customer lifecycle prepares the original published Baserow candidate, receives its complete SF100 dataset and selected files, copies the complete client and customer package, and invokes this operator in its existing application directory. See the Baserow customer's README for the selected run/candidate, query and original operation arguments.

The stable Ruby entry is:

~~~ruby
require "/absolute/customer-client/baserow/customer/baserow_customer_receiving"
require "/absolute/customer-client/developer/ruby-client/examples/rails_dataset/operator/commission"

result = Starforge::DatasetOperator::Commission.run(
  customer_directory: "/private/complete-baserow-delivery",
  manifest_sha256: original_baserow_delivery_manifest_sha256,
  directory: "/private/customer-application",
  source_key: original_source_key,
  record_id_column: original_record_id_output_alias
)

reopened = Starforge::DatasetOperator::Commission.reopen(
  directory: "/private/customer-application"
)
raise "Changed application" unless reopened == result
~~~

Use the original customer package's source key and projected record-ID alias. The mapping is derived from the actual native column metadata. Integer and Boolean columns retain their types; number values use exact decimal text; original record IDs form the unique tenant business key. All received rows are imported into the commissioner's actual SQLite database.

The commissioner uses a real Rails application and its middleware. It follows rendered forms through HTTP Basic authentication, session CSRF and signed selections, executes the actual import jobs, reads every change page, downloads complete exports and edition receipts, follows all original attachment references, and refreshes from saved source after the import. It then disconnects and reopens the application, verifies the full original receipt and current database records, and repeats the rendered receiving flow. A failure raises; completion returns schema `stellar-forge.baserow-rails-operator-application.v1` with state `COMPLETE`, the exact observed result and every retained application's relative file descriptor.

Rails 7.1 or later supplies Action Pack, Active Job, Nokogiri and Rack. The original native receiving lifecycle supplies Active Record and SQLite. Run with the same compatible bundle as the receiving application. The optional interactive server also uses the ordinary `rackup` and `puma` gems.

## Open the commissioned application in a browser

Load the copied provider class and start the included local server:

~~~sh
ruby -r /absolute/customer-client/baserow/customer/baserow_customer_receiving \
  /absolute/customer-client/developer/ruby-client/examples/rails_dataset/operator/install.rb \
  --directory /private/customer-application --port 9292
~~~

Open `http://127.0.0.1:9292/dataset_imports`. The HTTP Basic user is `operator`; the password is the application's private `access-key` file. The server binds to loopback. The complete application directory contains the original received customer, SQLite database, mappings, both reviews, original source copies, complete downloads, rendered receiving pages and completion result. Keep that directory private.

The commissioner uses inline jobs so its one process can complete the real journey. An existing application uses its own configured queue and authentication, as described below.

## Install in an existing Rails application

The host keeps its original database, target models, authentication, tenant policy and job queue. Copy or vendor the complete native client source. Apply the original dataset-history migration in the same database as the target records. See the parent Rails example for model and mapping definitions.

Include the concern in a controller that inherits from the host's authenticated application controller:

~~~ruby
require Rails.root.join("vendor/starforge/examples/rails_dataset/operator/controller")

class DatasetImportsController < ApplicationController
  include Starforge::DatasetOperator::Controller

  private

  def starforge_dataset_authorize!
    # Call the host's actual import permission policy here.
    # This example assumes the application supplies authorize!.
    authorize!(:manage_dataset_imports, current_account)
  end

  def starforge_dataset_tenant_key
    current_account.id.to_s
  end

  def starforge_dataset_actor
    current_user.id.to_s
  end
end
~~~

All three methods are required. The concern's default methods raise until the application supplies its actual context. Read and write actions pass through that same policy. The host's CSRF/session middleware stays enabled. Signed selections bind the source, review, tenant and operator for 24 hours.

Add routes:

~~~ruby
resources :dataset_imports, only: [:index, :show, :create] do
  collection { get :stylesheet }
  member do
    post :prepare
    post :refresh
    post :commit
    get :changes
    get :history
    get :attachments
    get :download
    get :receipt
    get :attachment
    get :handoff
  end
end
~~~

Configure the shared resolver during application boot so web requests and workers reconstruct the same authorized context. The following uses the supplied example models; replace the target scope and catalogue with the application's actual model relation and received-delivery records:

~~~ruby
Starforge::DatasetOperator.workspace_resolver = lambda do |tenant_key|
  Starforge::DatasetOperator::Workspace.new(
    directory: Rails.root.join("storage/dataset-operator").to_s,
    tenant_key: tenant_key,
    streams: Starforge::DatasetExample::DatasetStream.where(tenant_key: tenant_key),
    target_scope: ->(_stream) {
      Starforge::DatasetExample::CatalogRecord.where(tenant_key: tenant_key)
    },
    models: Starforge::DatasetExample::MODELS,
    catalog: -> {
      # Server-side records selected from the actual received-delivery inbox.
      received_dataset_candidates_for(tenant_key)
    },
    formats: {
      "baserow" => ->(directory, sha) {
        Starforge::BaserowCustomerDelivery.open(
          directory: directory, expected_manifest_sha256: sha
        )
      }
    }
  )
end
~~~

Create the `storage` parent directory privately before use. The operator creates its own private root and per-tenant review directories. Web and background workers need access to the same private filesystem and database. Configure a durable Active Job adapter in the host; preserve the original review directory while an operation is queued or running.

Each catalogue candidate is a server-controlled object:

~~~ruby
{
  id: "customer-source-edition-3",
  title: "Customer catalogue / received edition 3",
  stream_id: original_dataset_stream.id,
  directory: "/private/complete-received-customer",
  format: "baserow", # "dataset" opens a standalone original DatasetDelivery
  manifest_sha256: original_complete_manifest_sha256,
  mapping: original_application_mapping
}
~~~

A candidate can supply `mapping_path` instead of a mapping object. The browser receives signed selections; it cannot choose arbitrary filesystem paths or a target model. Each tenant stream is checked against the resolver's original scoped relation.

## Daily operation

1. **Prepare complete review.** Select a candidate in the inbox. The job copies the full delivery and mapping into its own review, then writes the complete preview before deriving browser pages and exports.
2. **Inspect all changes.** Page through inserted, updated, unchanged or removed rows and the adoption, restoration and source-change flags. Every row retains its exact typed before/after values, business key and original JSON.
3. **Approve and import.** The signed form selects this exact preview. The original importer rechecks the source, mapping, scope, database schema and current records inside its transaction, applying normal validations and callbacks.
4. **Resume an interruption.** Preparation and import reuse the review ID and original operation key. A lost queue response can be retried on that same review. If the database committed before receipt export completed, retry finishes the original receipt.
5. **Refresh from saved source.** This creates a new review from the current review's copied delivery and mapping. It continues to work after the producer's directory moves or disappears. Current application records determine the new preview.
6. **Receive the result.** Download complete JSON/CSV reviews, selected mapping, all historical edition rows, original files or the complete review TAR. History is scoped to the original dataset stream.

A changed application preview produces a conflict and keeps the original review available. Use “Refresh from saved source” to review the new current state. Errors appear with the same original review; queue transport errors retain a resume action.

## Files, editions and attachment identity

A review saves its original selection, a complete source copy, complete preview bundle, JSON/CSV review, indexed JSONL rows, original mapping, approval and committed receipt. The preview bundle is retained before derived exports, so a partial write resumes the exact reviewed rows even if application records later change. Large outputs stream through temporary files and are fully hashed before exposure.

Attachment pages retain every selected row/field/index reference from the complete Baserow customer package. A download must match one of those original references. The same physical file can serve several original references without duplicating its source bytes. All values in the HTML are escaped, and attachments download as binary files.

Every edition remains in the application's original dataset history tables. Historical receipt downloads verify and stream every retained row in that edition. The complete review TAR contains a relative manifest and the original received source, mapping, full preview, approval and available receipt. Use the host application's existing source deployment and database backup to transfer its wider application.

## Portable application receiving

`Commission.reopen` uses the application's own copied customer, mapping and database. It checks the complete retained file set before opening the original models, verifies the original import operation and every receipt row, verifies all current target rows, opens the same rendered screens and downloads the full receipt. Its return equals the original completed result.

For a commissioned delivery, copy the whole private application directory with its file modes preserved. Open the copy using the same complete delivered client source. The saved review selections retain original provenance, while subsequent access resolves the copy's own received directories and SQLite database. The provider lifecycle performs this step and temporarily parks its own producer artifacts to exercise offline receiving.

The first successful commissioning result is immutable. Operating the copied application further naturally creates new reviews or editions; the original completion result then describes its original received edition. Preserve that completed delivery and use the host's normal application backup when transferring later work.

## Export compatibility

New native exports contain the original 16-file client plus these 14 operator files. New seller exports contain the original 26-file client plus the operator. Inspect and copy continue to accept the original 8-, 21-, 26- and 16-file completed editions using their exact original manifests.

If a native export stopped after creating an empty private directory but before saving its source selection, `native-resume` initializes that empty directory with the currently selected complete source. A nonempty interrupted package requires its original retained source selection. Existing files are never silently replaced.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Commission the original received Baserow dataset through a real Rails app.
require "cgi"
require "uri"
require "rack/mock"
require "nokogiri"
require_relative "../../native_dataset_lifecycle"
require_relative "install"

module Starforge
  module DatasetOperator
    module Commission
      SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.baserow-rails-operator-application.v1"
      RESULT = "operator-result.json"
      ACTOR = "commissioning-operator"
      module_function

      # The compound Baserow class lives in the delivered customer's original
      # provider subtree, and is required by its lifecycle before this entry.
      def customer(directory,sha)
        Files.need(defined?(Starforge::BaserowCustomerDelivery),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_BASEROW_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED")
        BaserowCustomerDelivery.open(directory: directory,expected_manifest_sha256: sha)
      end

      def descriptor(root,path)
        value = NativeDatasetLifecycle.file_descriptor(path)
        value.delete("path")
        value.merge("name"=>path.delete_prefix(root + File::SEPARATOR))
      end

      def configuration(root)
        value = Store.read(File.join(root,"application.json"))
        Files.need(value["schema"] == SCHEMA && value["tenant_key"] == NativeDatasetLifecycle::TENANT &&
          HASH.match?(value["manifest_sha256"].to_s) && value["source_key"].is_a?(String) &&
          !value["source_key"].empty? && value["record_id_column"].is_a?(String),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION")
        value
      end

      def open_workspace(directory)
        root = Files.directory(directory)
        config = configuration(root)
        package = customer(File.join(root,"customer"),config.fetch("manifest_sha256"))
        mapping = Store.read(File.join(root,"mapping.json"))
        Files.need(mapping == NativeDatasetLifecycle.mapping_for(package.dataset,[config.fetch("record_id_column")]),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_MAPPING_CHANGED")
        NativeDatasetLifecycle.connect(File.join(root,"application.sqlite3"))
        streams = DatasetExample::DatasetStream.where(tenant_key: config.fetch("tenant_key"))
        stream = streams.find_by!(name: config.fetch("source_key"))
        Workspace.new(directory: File.join(root,"operator"),tenant_key: config.fetch("tenant_key"),
          streams: streams,target_scope: lambda { |_stream|
            NativeDatasetLifecycle::SourceRow.where(tenant_key: config.fetch("tenant_key"))
          },models: DatasetExample::MODELS,
          catalog: lambda {
            [{"id"=>"received-baserow","title"=>"Baserow customer delivery","stream_id"=>stream.id,
              "directory"=>File.join(root,"customer"),"format"=>"baserow",
              "manifest_sha256"=>config.fetch("manifest_sha256"),"mapping"=>mapping}]
          },formats: {"baserow"=>lambda { |folder,sha| customer(folder,sha) }})
      end

      def open_application(directory)
        root = Files.directory(directory)
        workspace = open_workspace(root)
        access_key = Files.read(File.join(root,"access-key"),1024).strip
        Installation.open(directory: root,workspace: workspace,access_key: access_key)
      end

      class Response
        attr_reader :status,:headers
        def initialize(status,headers,body)
          @status,@headers = status,headers.transform_keys { |key| key.to_s.downcase }
          @file = Tempfile.new(["dataset-operator-http-",".response"])
          @file.binmode
          @file.unlink
          body.each { |bytes| @file.write(bytes) }
          @file.flush
          @file.rewind
        rescue Exception
          @file&.close
          raise
        ensure
          body.close if body.respond_to?(:close)
        end
        def body
          Files.need(@file.size <= 64 * 1024 * 1024,"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTML_TOO_LARGE")
          @file.rewind
          @file.read.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
        end
        def save(path)
          # An interrupted commission may have retained the first signed HTML.
          # Keep that exact first response; final descriptors verify it on reopen.
          return if Store.present?(path)
          @file.rewind
          Store.write(path) { |out| IO.copy_stream(@file,out) }
        end
        def matches?(expected)
          @file.rewind
          digest,count = Digest::SHA256.new,0
          while (bytes = @file.read(1_048_576))
            digest.update(bytes)
            count += bytes.bytesize
          end
          count == expected.fetch("bytes") && digest.hexdigest == expected.fetch("sha256")
        end
        def close
          @file.close unless @file.closed?
        end
      end

      # Exercise the real middleware, authentication, CSRF, signed selections,
      # rendered views and streamed responses, using the actual received rows.
      class Session
        def initialize(application,access_key)
          @application,@access_key,@cookies = application,access_key,{}
        end
        def request(method,path,params: {},status: 200)
          input = method == "GET" ? "" : URI.encode_www_form(params)
          path += (path.include?("?") ? "&" : "?") + URI.encode_www_form(params) if method == "GET" && !params.empty?
          env = Rack::MockRequest.env_for("http://localhost" + path,
            method: method,input: input,"CONTENT_TYPE"=>"application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
            "HTTP_HOST"=>"localhost","HTTP_ORIGIN"=>"http://localhost",
            "HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"=>"Basic " + ["operator:" + @access_key].pack("m0"),
            "HTTP_COOKIE"=>@cookies.map { |name,value| name + "=" + value }.join("; "))
          native_status,headers,body = @application.call(env)
          response = Response.new(native_status,headers,body)
          Array(response.headers["set-cookie"]).flat_map { |value| value.split("\n") }.each do |line|
            name,value = line.split(";",2).first.split("=",2)
            @cookies[name] = value if name && value
          end
          RailsDataset.need(response.status == status,"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTTP_STATUS",
            method: method,path: path,expected: status,actual: response.status)
          if block_given?
            begin
              yield response
            ensure
              response.close
            end
          else
            response
          end
        rescue Exception
          response&.close
          raise
        end
      end

      def form(html,action)
        document = Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(html)
        chosen = document.css("form").find { |node| URI.parse(node["action"].to_s).path == action }
        Files.need(chosen,"DATASET_OPERATOR_RENDERED_FORM")
        values = chosen.css("input[name]").each_with_object({}) do |input,out|
          out[input["name"]] = input["value"].to_s
        end
        Files.need(values["authenticity_token"] && !values["authenticity_token"].empty?,
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_CSRF_FORM")
        values.reject { |key,_| %w[commit utf8].include?(key) }
      end

      def original_selection(root,values,purpose,filename)
        verifier = Rails.application.message_verifier("starforge-dataset-operator")
        selected = verifier.verified(values.fetch("selection"),purpose: purpose)
        Files.need(selected.is_a?(Hash) && selected["actor"] == ACTOR &&
          selected["tenant"] == NativeDatasetLifecycle::TENANT,"DATASET_OPERATOR_RENDERED_SELECTION")
        file = File.join(root,filename)
        if Store.present?(file)
          selected = Store.read(file)
          Files.need(selected["actor"] == ACTOR && selected["tenant"] == NativeDatasetLifecycle::TENANT &&
            selected["payload"].is_a?(Hash),"DATASET_OPERATOR_ORIGINAL_SELECTION")
        else
          Files.once(file,Files.json(selected))
        end
        # Reissue the same selected operation if its original 24-hour form expired.
        # The original payload is saved before the first HTTP mutation.
        values["selection"] = verifier.generate(selected,purpose: purpose,expires_in: 24.hours)
        [values,selected.fetch("payload")]
      end

      def show(session,id,save: nil)
        text = nil
        session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id) do |response|
          response.save(save) if save
          text = response.body
        end
        text
      end

      def file_set(root)
        out = []
        visit = lambda do |directory|
          Dir.children(directory).sort.each do |name|
            next if name.start_with?(".") || (directory == root && name == RESULT)
            path = File.join(directory,name)
            stat = File.lstat(path)
            Files.need(!stat.symlink? && stat.uid == Process.uid && (stat.mode & 0077).zero?,
              "DATASET_OPERATOR_PRIVATE_APPLICATION")
            if stat.directory?
              visit.call(Files.directory(path))
            else
              Files.need(stat.file?,"DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_FILE")
              out << descriptor(root,path)
            end
          end
        end
        visit.call(root)
        out
      end

      def journey(root,workspace,session)
        screens = Files.directory(File.join(root,"screens"),create: true)
        downloads = Files.directory(File.join(root,"downloads"),create: true)
        values = nil
        session.request("GET","/dataset_imports") do |response|
          response.save(File.join(screens,"inbox.html"))
          values = form(response.body,"/dataset_imports")
        end
        values,selected = original_selection(root,values,"create","create-selection.json")
        id = selected.fetch("review_id")
        chosen_path = File.join(workspace.path(id,create: true),"selection.json")
        unless Store.present?(chosen_path)
          session.request("POST","/dataset_imports",params: values,status: 303) {}
        end
        # A lost initial job response resumes the same selected review.
        unless Store.present?(File.join(workspace.path(id),"review.json"))
          html = show(session,id)
          resume_values = form(html,"/dataset_imports/" + id + "/prepare")
          session.request("POST","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/prepare",params: resume_values,status: 303) {}
        end
        ready = workspace.review(id)
        review_html = show(session,id,save: File.join(screens,"review.html"))
        GROUPS.each do |group|
          count = ready.fetch("groups").fetch(group).fetch("count")
          pages = [1,(count + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE].max
          pages.times do |page|
            session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/changes",params: {group: group,page: page}) do |response|
              response.save(File.join(screens,format("changes-%s-%06d.html",group,page)))
            end
          end
        end
        ready.fetch("files").each do |file|
          session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/download",params: {name: file.fetch("name")}) do |response|
            Files.need(response.matches?(file),"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTTP_EXPORT_CHANGED")
            response.save(File.join(downloads,file.fetch("name")))
          end
        end
        unless Store.present?(File.join(workspace.path(id),"committed.json"))
          commit_values = form(review_html,"/dataset_imports/" + id + "/commit")
          session.request("POST","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/commit",params: commit_values,status: 303) {}
        end
        detail = workspace.detail(id)
        Files.need(detail["committed"],"DATASET_OPERATOR_IMPORT_INCOMPLETE")
        committed = detail.fetch("committed")
        session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/download",params: {name: "receipt.json"}) do |response|
          Files.need(response.matches?(committed.fetch("file")),"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTTP_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
          response.save(File.join(downloads,"receipt.json"))
        end
        show(session,id,save: File.join(screens,"committed.html"))
        editions,before = 0,nil
        loop do
          params = before ? {before: before} : {}
          session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/history",params: params) do |response|
            response.save(File.join(screens,format("history-%06d.html",editions)))
          end
          history = workspace.history(id,before: before)
          history.fetch("items").each do |edition|
            native = workspace.historical_receipt(id,edition.fetch("id"))
            begin
              expected = {"bytes"=>native.bytes,"sha256"=>native.sha256}
              session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/receipt",params: {edition_id: edition.fetch("id")}) do |response|
                Files.need(response.matches?(expected),"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTTP_EDITION_CHANGED")
                response.save(File.join(downloads,"edition-" + edition.fetch("id") + ".json"))
              end
            ensure
              native.close
            end
            editions += 1
          end
          before = history["next_before"]
          break unless before
        end
        attachment_files,attachment_links,offset = 0,0,0
        loop do
          page = workspace.attachments(id,offset: offset)
          session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/attachments",params: {offset: offset}) do |response|
            response.save(File.join(screens,format("attachments-%06d.html",offset)))
          end
          page.fetch("files").each do |file|
            file.fetch("references").each do |reference|
              parameters = {file: file.fetch("file"),record_id: reference.fetch("record_id"),
                column: reference.fetch("column")}
              session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/attachment",params: parameters) do |response|
                Files.need(response.matches?(file),"DATASET_OPERATOR_HTTP_ATTACHMENT_CHANGED")
              end
              attachment_links += 1
            end
            attachment_files += 1
          end
          offset = page["next_offset"]
          break unless offset
        end
        session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/handoff") do |response|
          response.save(File.join(downloads,"review-handoff.tar"))
        end
        # Refresh from the review's own received source after the database commit.
        html = show(session,id)
        values = form(html,"/dataset_imports/" + id + "/refresh")
        values,refresh = original_selection(root,values,"refresh","refresh-selection.json")
        refreshed_id = refresh.fetch("review_id")
        unless Store.present?(File.join(workspace.path(refreshed_id,create: true),"selection.json"))
          session.request("POST","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/refresh",params: values,status: 303) {}
        end
        unless Store.present?(File.join(workspace.path(refreshed_id),"review.json"))
          html = show(session,refreshed_id)
          resume_values = form(html,"/dataset_imports/" + refreshed_id + "/prepare")
          session.request("POST","/dataset_imports/" + refreshed_id + "/prepare",params: resume_values,status: 303) {}
        end
        refreshed = workspace.review(refreshed_id)
        show(session,refreshed_id,save: File.join(screens,"saved-source-review.html"))
        package = workspace.selected_delivery(id)
        current = NativeDatasetLifecycle.verify_current_targets(workspace.importer(id),package.dataset)
        Files.need(refreshed.fetch("summary").fetch("counts") == current.fetch("counts") &&
          refreshed.fetch("summary").fetch("row_count") == package.dataset.row_count,
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_REFRESH_CHANGED")
        {"review_id"=>id,"refreshed_review_id"=>refreshed_id,"row_count"=>package.dataset.row_count,
          "preview"=>ready.fetch("summary"),"committed"=>committed,"current"=>current,
          "history_editions"=>editions,"attachment_files"=>attachment_files,"attachment_links"=>attachment_links}
      end

      def run(customer_directory:,manifest_sha256:,directory:,source_key:,record_id_column:)
        old_umask = File.umask(0077)
        root = Files.directory(File.expand_path(directory),create: true)
        Files.lock(root) do
          selected = {"schema"=>SCHEMA,"tenant_key"=>NativeDatasetLifecycle::TENANT,
            "manifest_sha256"=>manifest_sha256,"source_key"=>source_key,"record_id_column"=>record_id_column}
          Files.need(HASH.match?(manifest_sha256.to_s) && source_key.is_a?(String) &&
            !source_key.empty? && source_key.bytesize <= 128 && record_id_column.is_a?(String),
            "DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_SELECTION")
          Files.once(File.join(root,"application.json"),Files.json(selected))
          return reopen_locked(root) if Store.present?(File.join(root,RESULT))
          receiver = File.join(root,"customer")
          unless Store.present?(File.join(receiver,"baserow-delivery.json"))
            customer(Files.directory(customer_directory),manifest_sha256).copy_to(receiver)
          end
          package = customer(receiver,manifest_sha256)
          Files.need(package.dataset.fields.include?(record_id_column),"DATASET_OPERATOR_RECORD_ID_COLUMN")
          mapping = NativeDatasetLifecycle.mapping_for(package.dataset,[record_id_column])
          Files.once(File.join(root,"mapping.json"),Files.json(mapping))
          key_file = File.join(root,"access-key")
          Files.once(key_file,SecureRandom.hex(32) + "\n") unless Store.present?(key_file)
          database = File.join(root,"application.sqlite3")
          Files.once(database,"") unless Store.present?(database)
          NativeDatasetLifecycle.initialize_database(database,package.dataset,mapping)
          DatasetExample::DatasetStream.find_or_create_by!(
            tenant_key: NativeDatasetLifecycle::TENANT,name: source_key)
          workspace = open_workspace(root)
          application = Installation.open(directory: root,workspace: workspace,
            access_key: Files.read(key_file,1024).strip)
          session = Session.new(application,Files.read(key_file,1024).strip)
          observed = journey(root,workspace,session)
          NativeDatasetLifecycle.disconnect
          result = selected.merge("state"=>"COMPLETE","observed"=>observed,"files"=>file_set(root))
          Files.once(File.join(root,RESULT),Files.json(result))
          reopen_locked(root)
        end
      ensure
        NativeDatasetLifecycle.disconnect
        File.umask(old_umask) if old_umask
      end

      def reopen_locked(root)
        result = Store.read(File.join(root,RESULT))
        Files.need(result["schema"] == SCHEMA && result["state"] == "COMPLETE" &&
          result.slice("schema","tenant_key","manifest_sha256","source_key","record_id_column") == configuration(root),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_RESULT")
        Files.need(result.fetch("files") == file_set(root),"DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_CHANGED")
        workspace = open_workspace(root)
        observed = result.fetch("observed")
        id = observed.fetch("review_id")
        detail = workspace.detail(id)
        Files.need(detail.fetch("committed") == observed.fetch("committed") &&
          detail.fetch("review").fetch("summary") == observed.fetch("preview"),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_EDITION_CHANGED")
        selected = workspace.selection(id)
        NativeDatasetLifecycle.verify_complete_receipt(workspace.importer(id),selected.fetch("operation_key"),
          observed.fetch("committed").fetch("file"))
        package = workspace.selected_delivery(id)
        current = NativeDatasetLifecycle.verify_current_targets(workspace.importer(id),package.dataset)
        Files.need(current == observed.fetch("current"),"DATASET_OPERATOR_CURRENT_ROWS_CHANGED")
        refreshed = workspace.review(observed.fetch("refreshed_review_id"))
        Files.need(refreshed.fetch("summary").fetch("counts") == current.fetch("counts"),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_REFRESH_CHANGED")
        application = Installation.open(directory: root,workspace: workspace,
          access_key: Files.read(File.join(root,"access-key"),1024).strip)
        session = Session.new(application,Files.read(File.join(root,"access-key"),1024).strip)
        %w[/dataset_imports /dataset_imports/stylesheet].each do |path|
          session.request("GET",path) {}
        end
        %W[/dataset_imports/#{id} /dataset_imports/#{id}/changes /dataset_imports/#{id}/history
          /dataset_imports/#{id}/attachments /dataset_imports/#{observed.fetch("refreshed_review_id")}].each do |path|
          session.request("GET",path) {}
        end
        session.request("GET","/dataset_imports/" + id + "/download",params: {name: "receipt.json"}) do |response|
          Files.need(response.matches?(observed.fetch("committed").fetch("file")),
            "DATASET_OPERATOR_REOPEN_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
        end
        NativeDatasetLifecycle.disconnect
        Files.need(result.fetch("files") == file_set(root),"DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_CHANGED")
        result
      ensure
        NativeDatasetLifecycle.disconnect
      end

      def reopen(directory:)
        root = Files.directory(directory)
        Files.lock(root) { reopen_locked(root) }
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Include in an authenticated controller of the existing Rails application.
require "active_support/concern"
require_relative "jobs"

module Starforge
  module DatasetOperator
    module Controller
      extend ActiveSupport::Concern
      included do
        before_action :starforge_dataset_authorize!
        before_action :operator_context
        protect_from_forgery with: :exception
        append_view_path File.join(__dir__,"views")
        after_action do
          response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
          response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
        end
        helper_method :operator_token, :operator_values, :operator_text
        rescue_from Starforge::Error, Starforge::RailsDataset::ImportError, with: :operator_error
        rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
          head :not_found
        end
      end

      def index
        @candidates = @workspace.candidates
        @reviews = @workspace.list(before: params[:before])
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/index", layout: "starforge_dataset_operator"
      end

      def create
        selected = operator_verify("create")
        id = selected.fetch("review_id")
        @workspace.select(id: id, candidate_id: selected.fetch("candidate_id"),
          selection_sha256: selected.fetch("selection_sha256"), actor: @operator_actor)
        operator_enqueue(PrepareJob,id)
        redirect_to({action: :show,id: id},status: :see_other)
      end

      def show
        @detail = @workspace.detail(params[:id])
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/show", layout: "starforge_dataset_operator"
      end

      def prepare
        id = params[:id].to_s
        @workspace.selection(id)
        operator_enqueue(PrepareJob,id)
        redirect_to({action: :show,id: id},status: :see_other)
      end

      def refresh
        chosen = operator_verify("refresh")
        id = params[:id].to_s
        Files.need(chosen["original_review_id"] == id, "DATASET_OPERATOR_SELECTION_CHANGED")
        new_id = chosen.fetch("review_id")
        @workspace.refresh(id,new_id: new_id,actor: @operator_actor)
        operator_enqueue(PrepareJob,new_id)
        redirect_to({action: :show,id: new_id},status: :see_other)
      end

      def commit
        chosen = operator_verify("commit")
        id = params[:id].to_s
        Files.need(chosen["review_id"] == id, "DATASET_OPERATOR_SELECTION_CHANGED")
        @workspace.approve(id,preview_sha256: chosen.fetch("preview_sha256"),actor: @operator_actor)
        operator_enqueue(ImportJob,id)
        redirect_to({action: :show,id: id},status: :see_other)
      end

      def changes
        @detail = @workspace.detail(params[:id])
        @changes = @workspace.changes(params[:id],group: params.fetch(:group,"all"),
          page: operator_integer(:page,0))
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/changes", layout: "starforge_dataset_operator"
      end

      def history
        @detail = @workspace.detail(params[:id])
        @history = @workspace.history(params[:id],before: params[:before])
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/history", layout: "starforge_dataset_operator"
      end

      def attachments
        @detail = @workspace.detail(params[:id])
        @attachments = @workspace.attachments(params[:id],offset: operator_integer(:offset,0))
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/attachments", layout: "starforge_dataset_operator"
      end

      def download
        operator_download(@workspace.export(params[:id],params[:name].to_s))
      end

      def receipt
        operator_download(@workspace.historical_receipt(params[:id],params[:edition_id].to_s))
      end

      def attachment
        operator_download(@workspace.attachment(params[:id],file: params[:file].to_s,
          record_id: params[:record_id].to_s,column: params[:column].to_s))
      end

      def handoff
        operator_download(@workspace.handoff(params[:id]))
      end

      def stylesheet
        render plain: File.binread(File.join(__dir__,"operator.css")), content_type: "text/css"
      end

      private

      # Implement all three methods in the including application controller.
      # Its normal session/authentication helpers and role policy remain in force.
      def starforge_dataset_authorize!
        raise NotImplementedError, "Authorize dataset operator access in the application controller"
      end
      def starforge_dataset_tenant_key
        raise NotImplementedError, "Resolve the authenticated application's tenant"
      end
      def starforge_dataset_actor
        raise NotImplementedError, "Resolve the authenticated application's operator identity"
      end

      def operator_context
        @operator_tenant = starforge_dataset_tenant_key.to_s
        @operator_actor = starforge_dataset_actor.to_s
        Files.need(!@operator_actor.empty?, "DATASET_OPERATOR_ACTOR_REQUIRED")
        @workspace = DatasetOperator.workspace(@operator_tenant)
      end

      def operator_token(payload,purpose)
        Rails.application.message_verifier("starforge-dataset-operator").generate(
          {"tenant"=>@operator_tenant,"actor"=>@operator_actor,"payload"=>payload},
          purpose: purpose, expires_in: 24.hours)
      end

      def operator_verify(purpose)
        value = Rails.application.message_verifier("starforge-dataset-operator").verified(
          params[:selection].to_s,purpose: purpose)
        Files.need(value.is_a?(Hash) && value["tenant"] == @operator_tenant &&
          value["actor"] == @operator_actor && value["payload"].is_a?(Hash),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_SELECTION_EXPIRED")
        value.fetch("payload")
      end

      def operator_integer(name,default)
        value = params[name]
        value.nil? ? default : Integer(value.to_s,10)
      rescue ArgumentError
        raise ActionController::BadRequest, "Choose a whole-number page"
      end

      def operator_enqueue(job,id)
        result = job.perform_later(@operator_tenant,id)
        if result
          flash[:notice] = "The selected review is queued. Refresh this page for its result."
        else
          flash[:alert] = "The queue did not accept this review. Resume the same review below."
        end
      rescue StandardError
        # Queue transport may have accepted the job before its response was lost.
        # The retained review and importer make a repeat use the same operation.
        flash[:alert] = "The queue response was interrupted. Refresh this review; Resume keeps its original operation."
      end

      def operator_download(file)
        response.headers["Content-Type"] = file.content_type
        response.headers["Content-Length"] = file.bytes.to_s
        response.headers["Content-Disposition"] = ActionDispatch::Http::ContentDisposition.format(
          disposition: "attachment",filename: file.filename)
        response.headers["X-Content-SHA256"] = file.sha256
        self.response_body = file
      rescue Exception
        file&.close
        raise
      end

      def operator_error(error)
        @operator_problem = error.message
        render template: "starforge_dataset_operator/error",layout: "starforge_dataset_operator",status: :conflict
      end

      def operator_values(raw)
        value = RailsDataset.unpack(Files.parse(raw))
        value.is_a?(Hash) ? value : {"value"=>value}
      end

      def operator_text(value)
        case value
        when BigDecimal then value.to_s("F")
        when Time, DateTime then value.iso8601(9)
        when Date then value.iso8601
        when NilClass then "(null)"
        when String then value
        when Hash, Array then RailsDataset.exact_json(value)
        else value.to_s
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. A complete local commissioning application; existing applications include Controller.
require "rails"
require "action_controller/railtie"
require "active_job/railtie"
require "logger"
require "base64"
require_relative "controller"

module Starforge
  module DatasetOperator
    class CommissionApplication < Rails::Application
    end

    module Installation
      class << self
        attr_reader :tenant_key, :access_key, :application
        def open(directory:, workspace:, access_key:)
          Files.need(access_key.is_a?(String) && /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/.match?(access_key),
            "DATASET_OPERATOR_ACCESS_KEY")
          Files.need(!@application || @access_key == access_key,"DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_CHANGED")
          @tenant_key, @access_key = workspace.tenant_key, access_key
          DatasetOperator.workspace_resolver = lambda do |selected|
            Files.need(selected == workspace.tenant_key,"DATASET_OPERATOR_TENANT_CHANGED")
            workspace
          end
          unless @application
            application_class = CommissionApplication
            application_class.config.root = Pathname.new(directory)
            application_class.config.eager_load = false
            application_class.config.secret_key_base = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(access_key + "/rails-session") * 2
            application_class.config.logger = Logger.new(File::NULL)
            application_class.config.hosts = ["localhost","127.0.0.1","::1"]
            application_class.config.consider_all_requests_local = true
            application_class.config.action_dispatch.show_exceptions = :none
            application_class.config.action_controller.allow_forgery_protection = true
            application_class.config.session_store :cookie_store, key: "_starforge_dataset_operator"
            @application = application_class.instance
            @application.initialize!
            @application.routes.draw do
              resources :dataset_imports,controller: "starforge/dataset_operator/commission",only: [:index,:show,:create] do
                collection { get :stylesheet }
                member do
                  post :prepare
                  post :refresh
                  post :commit
                  get :changes
                  get :history
                  get :attachments
                  get :download
                  get :receipt
                  get :attachment
                  get :handoff
                end
              end
              root to: redirect("/dataset_imports")
            end
          end
          Rails.application = @application
          # Commissioning performs the actual jobs in this process. Production
          # installations use their application's configured durable queue.
          PrepareJob.queue_adapter = :inline
          ImportJob.queue_adapter = :inline
          @application
        end
      end
    end

    class CommissionController < ActionController::Base
      include Controller
      private
      def starforge_dataset_authorize!
        authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic("Dataset operator") do |user,password|
          user == "operator" && ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(
            Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(password.to_s),Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(Installation.access_key))
        end
      end
      def starforge_dataset_tenant_key
        Installation.tenant_key
      end
      def starforge_dataset_actor
        "commissioning-operator"
      end
    end
  end
end

if File.expand_path($PROGRAM_NAME) == File.expand_path(__FILE__)
  require "optparse"
  require_relative "commission"
  options = {port: 9292,bind: "127.0.0.1"}
  parser = OptionParser.new do |o|
    o.banner = "ruby install.rb --directory PRIVATE_APPLICATION [--port 9292] [--bind 127.0.0.1]"
    o.on("--directory PATH") { |value| options[:directory] = value }
    o.on("--port NUMBER",Integer) { |value| options[:port] = value }
    o.on("--bind ADDRESS") { |value| options[:bind] = value }
  end
  parser.parse!(ARGV)
  abort parser.to_s unless options[:directory] && ARGV.empty? &&
    (1..65535).cover?(options[:port]) && %w[127.0.0.1 ::1 localhost].include?(options[:bind])
  application = Starforge::DatasetOperator::Commission.open_application(options.fetch(:directory))

module Starforge
  module DatasetOperator

      queue_as :default

# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Private review and import workspace for the application's original dataset models.
require "securerandom"
require "fileutils"
require "rubygems/package"
require_relative "../models"

module Starforge
  module DatasetOperator
    UUID = /\A[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-4[a-f0-9]{3}-[89ab][a-f0-9]{3}-[a-f0-9]{12}\z/
    HASH = /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/
    PAGE_SIZE = 100
    GROUPS = %w[all inserted updated unchanged removed adopted restored source_changed].freeze

    # Resolve the same authorized application context in web requests and jobs.
    # The host application installs this resolver; it is never read from HTTP input.
    class << self
      attr_accessor :workspace_resolver
      def workspace(tenant_key)
        Files.need(workspace_resolver.respond_to?(:call), "DATASET_OPERATOR_RESOLVER_REQUIRED")
        result = workspace_resolver.call(tenant_key.to_s)
        Files.need(result.is_a?(Workspace) && result.tenant_key == tenant_key.to_s,
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_TENANT_CHANGED")
        result
      end
    end

    class Download
      attr_reader :bytes, :sha256, :filename, :content_type
      def initialize(filename:, content_type:)
        @filename, @content_type = filename, content_type
        @file = Tempfile.new(["dataset-operator-", ".download"])
        @file.binmode
        @file.unlink
        yield @file
        @file.flush
        @bytes = @file.size
        @file.rewind
        digest = Digest::SHA256.new
        chunk = nil
        digest.update(chunk) while (chunk = @file.read(1_048_576))
        @sha256 = digest.hexdigest
        @file.rewind
      rescue Exception
        @file&.close
        raise
      end
      def each
        return enum_for(__method__) unless block_given?
        @file.rewind
        chunk = nil
        yield chunk while (chunk = @file.read(1_048_576))
      ensure
        close if block_given?
      end
      def close
        @file&.close unless @file&.closed?
      end
    end

    module Store
      module_function
      def read(path)
        Files.parse(Files.read(path, 64 * 1024 * 1024))
      end
      def present?(path)
        File.exist?(path) || File.symlink?(path)
      end
      def replace(path, value)
        raw = Files.json(value)
        temp = Tempfile.new([".operator-state-", ".pending"], File.dirname(path))
        begin
          temp.binmode
          temp.write(raw)
          temp.flush
          temp.fsync
          if present?(path)
            stat = File.lstat(path)
            Files.need(stat.file? && !stat.symlink? && stat.uid == Process.uid &&
              (stat.mode & 0077).zero?, "DATASET_OPERATOR_STATE_CHANGED")
          end
          File.rename(temp.path, path)
          Files.sync(File.dirname(path))
        ensure
          temp.close!
        end
      end
      def write(path, &block)
        value = DatasetExample::Artifacts.write_once(path, &block)
        {"name"=>File.basename(path), "bytes"=>value.fetch("bytes"), "sha256"=>value.fetch("sha256")}
      end
      # Application previews and receipts can be larger than the original input.
      # Verify the whole selected file before exposing a row or download.
      def snapshot(path, expected)
        Files.need(expected.is_a?(Hash) && expected["bytes"].is_a?(Integer) &&
          expected["bytes"] >= 0 && HASH.match?(expected["sha256"].to_s),
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_FILE_DESCRIPTOR")
        temp = Tempfile.new(["dataset-operator-", ".snapshot"])
        begin
          temp.binmode
          temp.unlink
          File.open(path, File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::NONBLOCK) do |input|
            before = input.stat
            Files.need(before.file? && before.size == expected["bytes"], "DATASET_OPERATOR_FILE_CHANGED")
            digest, count = Digest::SHA256.new, 0
            while (chunk = input.read(1_048_576))
              count += chunk.bytesize
              Files.need(count <= expected["bytes"], "DATASET_OPERATOR_FILE_CHANGED")
              digest.update(chunk)
              temp.write(chunk)
            end
            after = input.stat
            Files.need(count == expected["bytes"] && digest.hexdigest == expected["sha256"] &&
              [before.dev,before.ino,before.size,before.mtime,before.ctime] ==
              [after.dev,after.ino,after.size,after.mtime,after.ctime], "DATASET_OPERATOR_FILE_CHANGED")
          end
          temp.flush
          temp.rewind
          yield temp
        ensure
          temp.close!
        end
      end
    end

    class Workspace
      attr_reader :tenant_key
      def initialize(directory:, tenant_key:, streams:, target_scope:, models:, catalog:, formats: {})
        Files.need(tenant_key.is_a?(String) && !tenant_key.empty? && tenant_key.bytesize <= 128,
          "DATASET_OPERATOR_TENANT_REQUIRED")
        Files.need(streams.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Relation) && target_scope.respond_to?(:call) &&
          catalog.respond_to?(:call), "DATASET_OPERATOR_APPLICATION_CONTEXT")
        @tenant_key, @streams, @target_scope, @models, @catalog = tenant_key, streams, target_scope, models, catalog
        root = Files.directory(directory, create: true)
        @directory = Files.directory(File.join(root, Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(tenant_key)), create: true)
        @formats = {"dataset"=>lambda { |directory, sha|
          DatasetDelivery.open(directory, expected_manifest_sha256: sha)
        }}.merge(formats.transform_keys(&:to_s))
        Files.need(@formats.values.all? { |opener| opener.respond_to?(:call) }, "DATASET_OPERATOR_FORMAT")
      end

      def candidates
        values = @catalog.call
        Files.need(values.is_a?(Array), "DATASET_OPERATOR_CATALOG")
        ids = Set.new
        values.map do |input|
          value = input.transform_keys(&:to_s)
          Files.need(value["id"].is_a?(String) && /\A[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}\z/.match?(value["id"]) &&
            ids.add?(value["id"]) && value["title"].is_a?(String) &&
            @formats.key?(value.fetch("format","dataset")) && HASH.match?(value["manifest_sha256"].to_s),
            "DATASET_OPERATOR_CANDIDATE")
          stream(value.fetch("stream_id"))
          mapping = value["mapping"]
          mapping = Files.parse(Files.read(value.fetch("mapping_path"))) if mapping.nil?
          Files.need(mapping.is_a?(Hash), "DATASET_OPERATOR_MAPPING")
          chosen = {"id"=>value["id"], "title"=>value["title"], "stream_id"=>value["stream_id"].to_s,
            "directory"=>Files.directory(value.fetch("directory")), "format"=>value.fetch("format","dataset"),
            "manifest_sha256"=>value["manifest_sha256"], "mapping"=>RailsDataset.copy_json(mapping)}
          chosen.merge("selection_sha256"=>RailsDataset.fingerprint(chosen))
        end
      end

      def stream(id)
        value = @streams.find(id)
        Files.need(value.tenant_key.to_s == @tenant_key, "DATASET_OPERATOR_TENANT_CHANGED")
        value
      end

      def path(id, create: false)
